root_idea.summary: The root centers on pushing something aside, removing it from a position, or turning it back.
root_idea.development: From physical propulsion and removal develop the senses of repelling harm, defending, delivering something onward to its recipient, mutual pushing, and forceful movement.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form دَفَعَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form III perfect citation form دَافَعَ.
Displayed under the singular masculine active-participle citation form دَافِعٌ.
Displayed as the verbal noun دَفْعٌ.

senses.definition: To push, drive, repel, remove, or turn back; to avert something harmful.
senses.usage_conditions: With عَنْ, the construction expresses averting harm or defending against it. The Quranic forms include commands to repel or ward off and a usage translated as defending.

senses.definition: To give, hand over, restore, or deliver something to its rightful recipient.
senses.usage_conditions: With إِلَى, the construction means to give or deliver to someone; this includes handing over property or a trust.

senses.definition: To defend or protect by actively repelling harm or attack.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْ for defending or protecting someone from harm; the Quranic usage presents defense as forceful repulsion.

senses.definition: A repeller, warder-off, or defender; one who prevents something from reaching or affecting another.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences use the word in negated constructions for there being no repeller or defender against an event.

senses.definition: Repelling, driving back, or checking an opposing force or people.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction of God’s دفع of people by means of others, the noun denotes the checking or prevention of aggression and disorder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single push, thrust, propulsion, or pouring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A unitary action or quantity derived from the Form I action; it can refer to one act of pushing or one outpouring from a vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel: to secrete the first milk in the udder shortly before giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression refers specifically to the pre-parturition accumulation or secretion of milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be driven away or pass from one party to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an intransitive or quasi-passive construction for something that departs from one group and is transferred or driven toward another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rebut, refute, or repel a statement with an argument, allegation, or proof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with speech, a claim, or an argument as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave someone or something alone, sparing it from interference.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An imperative expression meaning to desist from taking or troubling the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water or a torrent: to pour or gush forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in an intransitive construction in which the water is understood as propelling itself forward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press or push forward, especially in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is understood to propel itself onward through continued exertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people or company: to come or arrive all at once.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective body is treated as arriving in a single movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reach or lead to a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With إِلَى, the verb may describe a person reaching a destination or a road leading to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To depart from, leave, or journey away from a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe a person leaving a location or urging a riding animal onward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extended use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive, compel, or necessitate someone to undertake or resort to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The destination or resulting action is expressed with إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone abject, contemptible, or poor, as though fit to be driven away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or intensive Form II use describing the production of a degraded social state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To straighten or make a bow even.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical use applied to a bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contending or striving with another to push, repel, or push against one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III verbal noun can denote mutual physical resistance and is also often used for ordinary pushing or repelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To delay, defer, or put someone off concerning a right or due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes repeated postponement of delivering what is owed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To devote oneself to an affair and persist or exert oneself in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Form III use emphasizing continued application and perseverance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push, repel, or jostle one another, or to pass a thing or person from one to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VI reciprocal construction may describe mutual resistance in conflict or a group’s repeated refusal to accept responsibility for an object or guest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of two statements or sentences: to oppose, conflict with, or contradict one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative reciprocal use applied to mutually incompatible propositions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move or continue by successive impulses, one part propelling the next.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a torrent or of a horse’s running when motion proceeds in successive surges.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become propelled, driven, thrust, or carried away or onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VII verb is chiefly intransitive or quasi-passive and may describe movement away from a position or forward with impetus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To launch into, enter upon, or break forth into discourse or another activity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي for entering discourse, recitation, laughter, or a comparable activity with sudden momentum.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall eagerly to eating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with food as the activity entered upon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To proceed in an affair with penetrating energy, vigor, and effectiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي for vigorous engagement in an undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or beg for the repelling of evils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction expresses seeking the removal or averting of harm, especially by supplication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A body or party of people arriving at once.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective arrival treated as one incoming movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single uninterrupted burst or course of running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended unitary-use noun for one continuous exertion or rush.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity that pours forth at once: a gush, shower, fall, or rush of liquid, and by extension a surge of a torrent, troops, or night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes a discrete mass or surge issuing without interruption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion or allotment of property that is given.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distributive use referring to one share or payment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name for a ewe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the animal’s pushing its thigh from side to side because of bulkiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who or something that pushes, propels, repels, or defends vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a forceful person; of a she-camel, it can describe one that kicks backward when milked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who moves a bone aside in a bowl to make room for a piece of meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of the action of putting an obstacle aside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great surging mass or quantity, especially of water or people; a great force that propels another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of waves, torrents, seas, or a large crowd advancing in a pressing mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel: one that secretes the first milk in its udder shortly before giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participle use describing pre-parturition milk accumulation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lower watercourse or tributary channel that pours into another watercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes a subordinate channel or the lower part where water descends into a valley or another channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A channel or lower part of a valley through which water runs and disperses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote a watercourse or the outlet where a torrent pours forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument for pushing, propelling, or repelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term includes specialized instruments such as a cannon and an instrument used by midwives to protrude a fetus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A forceful or strongly supporting thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intensively in the expression رُكْنٌ مِدْفَعٌ, a strong corner or support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: one held in high estimation and spared from being ridden or loaded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: When brought near a load, the valued camel is sent back in order to preserve it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: one held in low estimation and sent back as despised.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the contrary camel-use to the honorific sense; the two values are explicitly reported as opposites.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poor, abject, or despised person whom people repel or pass from one to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe someone rejected by relatives or a guest whom members of a tribe each turn away to the next person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Driven, compelled, or necessitated to undertake or resort to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction expresses being forced toward an action or course of recourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unopposed in authority; not jostled, challenged, or displaced from leadership.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a chief whose position is not contested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized epithet or name derived from forceful resistance or defense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a saying: self-contradictory, with one part opposing another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative participial construction applied to internally conflicting speech.
